items.title: How one AI agent exposed five critical enterprise security gaps
items.snippet: An AI agent built to automate invoice processing could be manipulated into changing vendor bank details through a malicious email, without triggering traditional security alerts. Token Security examines five critical AI agent security gaps and shares practical guidance from industry security leaders on preventing them.
items.summary: Token Security says a malicious email could manipulate an invoice-processing AI agent into changing vendor bank details without triggering traditional security alerts.
items.why: Check whether AI-driven payment changes require independent verification and are visible in security monitoring.

items.title: TSMC confirms employee data breach tied to cloud service provider

items.summary: An investigation found TSMC systems were not compromised; the employee information matched data held by a cloud service provider and was unrelated to company operations or customer data.
items.why: Review what employee data cloud providers store and how access and incident investigations cover it.

learn.explainer: An AI agent is software designed to carry out tasks with some degree of automation. Here, an agent processes invoices, and a malicious email could manipulate it into changing vendor bank details.
A mine-hunting drone mothership is a vessel intended to serve as a platform for mine-hunting drones. The UK plans to buy three under an agreement with Norway.
Defense industrial cooperation means countries working together in defense-related industry. The article argues that expanding it could help defend U.S. alliances.

analysis.headline: Trust, access and resilience across systems and alliances
paragraphs: The top stories connect questions of trust and control across different settings. An invoice-processing AI agent could be manipulated through a malicious email, while the TSMC investigation links employee information to a cloud provider without finding TSMC systems compromised. ActiveCloud’s encrypted infrastructure, meanwhile, left customers without key services for days.

For defenders, these accounts suggest that security boundaries extend beyond an organization’s own systems: automated workflows, third-party data stores and cloud services all matter. Check how sensitive changes are verified, what information providers hold, and how continuity plans work when services are inaccessible. The reports do not establish that these incidents share a cause.

The other top stories point to strategic coordination and operational capability: a proposed UK purchase of mine-hunting drone motherships under a Norway agreement, and an argument for stronger U.S. alliance cooperation. Eisenkot’s task of forming a government adds a leadership dimension. Analysts should watch how these stated plans and political positions develop, without treating proposals or arguments as outcomes.
takeaways: Treat AI workflows and cloud providers as part of the security boundary.
Plan for critical services to become inaccessible, not only for data loss.
Track alliance proposals and leadership developments separately from confirmed outcomes.
